saints.name: Gregory the Wonderworker of Neocaesarea
saints.dates: Third century; born between 210 and 215 in the OCA life

summary.text: A third-century bishop and missionary in Pontus. Thaumaturgus means Wonderworker; this Gregory is distinct from the later Cappadocian saints.
summary.reason: A concise source-bound account of the saint's life, identity and death; the linked modern source is not reproduced in full.

saints.context: The Church's published hagiographic account is distinguished from independently established chronology. Unknown dates and circumstances are left unspecified.

blocks.text: The OCA places his birth between 210 and 215 in a prominent pagan family at Neocaesarea. Originally called Theodore, he became a Christian and studied under Origen.
blocks.reason: A concise source-bound account of the saint's life, identity and death; the linked modern source is not reproduced in full.

blocks.text: He became bishop of his home city. The received life depicts preaching, care for the needy, reconciliation of disputes, and protection of Christians during the Decian persecution of 249–251. Its miracle narratives explain his traditional title.

blocks.text: The OCA associates a Trinitarian confession with him and relates its reception by later Fathers. It also transmits the account that Christianity grew from a small minority to predominate in his city.
